content_units: A warm, low-tech evening for   24 adults   with a good mix of conversation, light movement, and team play. This program fits   18:30–21:30 EST  , stays   under CAD 180  , and is designed to work well for a mixed-age adult group.
Time   Activity   Format   Why it works   Est. Cost
18:30–18:45   Welcome Mixer: Paired Prompt Cards   Rotating pairs/small groups   Easy start, low pressure, helps guests mingle quickly   CAD 12
18:45–19:25   Team Trivia Relay   4 teams of 6   Social, funny, mentally engaging, can be fully seated   CAD 18
19:25–20:05   Collaborative Table Challenge   Small-group build/puzzle challenge   Cooperative rather than competitive; good for mixed ages   CAD 40
20:05–20:15   Break + refreshments reset   Unstructured   Buffer for transitions and late-running segments   CAD 0
20:15–21:00   Story Circle Game: “Pass the Plot”   Whole room, seated circle or tables   Creative, memorable, no special skill needed   CAD 10
21:00–21:30   Group Finale: Music Bingo or backup flex time   Seated whole-group game   Strong closing activity; easy to extend or shorten   CAD 35
Activity 1: Welcome Mixer — Paired Prompt Cards
- “What hobby would you start if time were free?”
- “What is a small thing that always improves your day?”
- Run 3 rounds of 4 minutes each, then 2 rounds in groups of 4.
- Best for easing people in without requiring performance.
- “Relay” element: one runner per team can deliver answers, but for accessibility this can also be a   table captain   instead of requiring walking.
- Goal: build or solve together in 25–30 minutes
- One person starts with a sentence.
- Use prompt slips like “At Union Station…”, “During a snowstorm…”, or “At a neighborhood bake sale…”
- Play short audio clips from well-known songs across eras, or if no audio setup is preferred, use lyric/theme bingo with a caller.
- Great closer because it is familiar, seated, and easy to scale.
- 4 answer sheets clipboards or table pads
- Trivia question sheets and score sheets
- Craft sticks / index cards / newspapers depending on challenge format
- Envelopes for puzzle clues if using puzzle version
- Optional tea, water, and simple snacks if the venue is not already covering refreshments
- Printed materials and name tags:   CAD 20
- Music bingo printouts and caller sheets:   CAD 15
This leaves a   CAD 10 cushion   under your   CAD 180   limit.
For the   two participants with limited mobility  , structure the room and activities so they can join fully without needing special treatment.
- Use   wide table spacing   and clear pathways between entrance, seating, washroom, and refreshments.
- Seat both participants where they can easily see/hear instructions and join team conversation.
- Keep all 4 activities   playable while seated  .
- Replace any “go to the front” or “run answers up” element with:
- Avoid floor-based tasks or materials placed low.
- Provide chairs with backs and a few firmer seats if available.
- Use   large-print handouts   for prompts, trivia, and bingo.
- Keep background music low or off during instructions.
- 1 refreshment station off to the side, not blocking circulation
Backup if an Activity Runs Short
If one segment ends early, use this quick backup.
- Keep participants in their table groups.
- Give them 5 minutes to find   8 things everyone at the table has in common  .
- No obvious basics like “we are all human”
- Encourage fun specifics: favorite comfort food, first concert decade, preferred season, etc.
- Then each table shares their best 2 answers.
- Easy to extend from 5 to 15 minutes
- The program is best paced with   alternating energy levels  : mingle → think → build → create/play.
- For ages   25–70  , cooperative and nostalgia-friendly activities usually land better than highly physical games.
- Keep instructions to   under 2 minutes   per activity to maintain flow.
- Ask one facilitator and one volunteer helper to manage timing, scoring, and mobility support.
